instrument.name: Narmada Nifty 50 Index Fund - Direct Plan - Growth

answers.question: What does it invest in and who runs it?

sentences.text: Narmada Nifty 50 Index Fund - Direct Plan - Growth is a Index Fund from Narmada Mutual Fund; its money is 99.7% in shares, 0.0% in debt and 0.3% in cash and similar assets.
It lists 50 companies in its portfolio, and the largest are Reliance Industries Ltd (9.5%), HDFC Bank Ltd (7.3%) and Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (6.0%).
It is run by Rohan Mehta; the longest-serving manager has been in charge for 7.3 years.

answers.question: How has it done against its benchmark and category over 3, 5 and 10 years?

sentences.text: Over the last 3 years the fund returned 6.9% a year, below its benchmark (Nifty 50 TRI) at 7.1% and the same as the Index Fund average of 6.8%.
Over the last 5 years the fund returned 6.1% a year, below its benchmark (Nifty 50 TRI) at 6.3% and above the Index Fund average of 5.8%.
The fund is younger than 10 years, so no figure is shown for that period.

answers.question: How bumpy has the ride been?

sentences.text: On ₹1 lakh, the fund's worst fall of 15.8% would have been about ₹15,808 between its high and its low point.
Over the same dates the worst fall in its benchmark was 15.7%, and the Index Fund average worst fall is 16.5%.
It had not got back to the earlier high by 30 Oct 2026.

answers.question: What does it cost per year on your amount?

sentences.text: On ₹1 lakh (an illustrative amount, since you do not hold this fund) the fund charges about ₹180 a year, an expense ratio of 0.2%; the Index Fund median for direct plans is 0.2%.
No direct or regular twin of this fund is known, so no plan comparison is shown.
The fee is taken out of the fund's value every day, so it is never billed to you separately.
